summary.intent: Run an adversarial review of Callisto PR #101 (self-release lifecycle rewrite) covering architecture, semantic model, performance, bugs, corner cases and black-box test coverage, then consolidate the results and the full release history into a handoff.
summary.outcome: Six parallel audits plus Codex findings turned up three live-verified P0 release blockers and about 60 other findings. PR #101 was hardened and merged, and two further workflow bugs were fixed (#103 merged, #104 open), but the 0.8.0 release was still not published at the end.

repo: Callisto test fakes in durable_release_e2e_tests.rs encode wrong provider semantics (cargo info says 'could not find' until publish, gh accepts any flag, target_commitish hard-coded to the SHA), so green CI could not catch real-provider bugs. The fix was captured real provider fixtures, strict fakes and real-tool flag contract tests.

GitHub Actions skips any job with a skipped transitive ancestor unless its own if: contains a status function such as always(). The release-candidate -> plan -> build-artifact -> execute chain was silently skipped because of this.
shasum run on one runner records absolute paths under that runner's RUNNER_TEMP, so a shasum -c on a different runner fails. Checksums must be generated from inside the handoff directory.

cargo info name@ver run inside a workspace reads the local manifest, not the registry, and needs an explicit --registry crates-io. gh api has no --repo flag. A GitHub Release created without --target reports target_commitish as the branch name, not the SHA.

Cargo builds took hours because target/debug/deps held 1.72M .o files from macOS split-debuginfo. A local git-excluded .cargo/config.toml with split-debuginfo=off fixed it, and a cold build is then about 31 s.
The release workflow's policy script (verify-release-workflow-policy.sh) has a --self-test mutant suite (30 mutants) and now includes a scheduler simulating GitHub's if:/needs semantics.
The CLI product tag moved to callisto@{version} (previously callisto-cli@*). Owner decision: migrate or add lookup compatibility via previous-tag-templates, do not revert.

Release flow design after hardening: GitHub Release created as draft, assets uploaded, then a final ForgePublish op. Provider observation goes through the package managers (cargo info, npm view). Registry endpoints are https only, and PyPI is refused at plan time.

code.finding: release execute ran all remote effects at line 382 before parsing --orchestration-revision (389) and the Hermetic-source check (395-402), so bad arguments could fail the command after publishing. Fixed by validating before effects.
Forge release observation required target_commitish == source SHA, but GitHub returns the default branch name, so the first real publish would classify as Conflict.

cargo_version_is_published runs cargo info from the workspace root without --registry for crates-io, so it reads the local manifest and reports unpublished versions as published. This leads to false AlreadySatisfied and a false terminal receipt in recovery.

derive_release_inputs folds a missing [release] and an unknown profile into Option::None, so prepared_registry_binding silently falls back to the production registry key. Profile enforcement lived only in the CLI.
CliCommandRunner::run is an unbounded Command::output() with no timeout. Only run_with_timeout_impl enforces the 10 MiB cap and a deadline, and most publish, push and gh calls used plain run.
The shared-destination isolation check compares raw URL and repo strings, so it is bypassable by case, port or .git. None == None also gives a false positive, and the check is pairwise only.
